correctness.rationale: Independent uniform-coordinate sampling gives D^2=sum s_i W_i with exact nonzero third cumulant of W. The three cumulants invert to power sums S_1,S_2,S_3, and Newton identities yield a cubic with precisely the positive squared edges. Positivity and the exact cubic discriminant prove the feasible moment region including strict degeneracy boundary. Explicit distinct boxes agree in M_2,M_4, but differ at M_6. A rigorous Rouché cluster-matching argument gives the global 1/3-Hölder bound, and same-first-two-moments families approaching cubes prove its exponent optimal. Exact rational code reproduces 2,197 sample triples without claiming finite testing as a universal proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed population observable is the first three even Euclidean distances between independent volume-uniform interior points in a three-dimensional rectangular solid. Archived forward cube and planar rectangle results do not explicitly recover three unequal lengths, prove the feasible normalized moment region, or a sharp inverse stability exponent. A directly relevant modern primary PDF gives an analogous three-cumulant reconstruction for random uniform-direction width, not this interior point-pair variable. Available source texts and semantic mathematical-record searches found no same-statement coverage; unresolved historic full text and unindexed literature are noted. The elementary positive cubic discriminant is credited as existing algebra, not claimed independently novel.
residual_risks: Full 1999 unit-cube paper unavailable in this run; its public abstract is narrower, but an inaccessible full text cannot establish complete noncoverage.
Other unindexed box inverse-distance literature may have an equivalent theorem; literature search is evidence, not proof of novelty.
The 2026 width paper was inspected in its inverse sections rather than read completely; the measured random variable is explicitly different.

value.rationale: The geometric inverse problem asks how much shape information survives unlabeled independent interior-point distances. Exactly three accessible scalar population moments suffice, exactly two lose a continuous shape family, and an explicit sharp feasible moment domain provides geometric consistency checks; optimal 1/3-Hölder stability reveals inevitable ill-conditioning near cubes. The combination is a natural complete finite-statistic geometric reconstruction, beyond a routine one-shape moment computation.
